name: Avelino Valencia
title: California State Assemblymember
district: California State Assembly District 68 (Anaheim, Santa Ana, Orange)
background: Valencia grew up in Orange County and attended local public schools. He earned an associate degree from Fullerton College, a bachelor's degree in political science from San Jose State University (where he played Division I college football), and a Master of Public Administration in government and policy from Johns Hopkins University in 2020.

Before running for office, Valencia worked as a special education instructional assistant in the Anaheim Elementary School District and coached football at Fullerton College. He then worked as a political staffer/chief deputy for then-Assemblymember Tom Daly from roughly 2016 to 2022, giving him direct experience inside the Assembly before he was ever elected to it.

Valencia was elected to the Anaheim City Council (District 4) in 2020, defeating Annemarie Randle-Trejo and Jeannine Robbins with just over 50 percent of the vote, and served on the council from 2020 to 2022. During that tenure he worked on COVID-19 vaccine distribution, mental health access, park development, and small-business support.

He was first elected to the California State Assembly in November 2022 to represent the newly drawn 68th Assembly District (Anaheim, Santa Ana, Orange), succeeding termed/redistricted-out incumbent Steven Choi, and was reelected in November 2024 with 63.7% of the vote against Republican Mike Tardif.

In December 2024, Valencia announced a campaign for California State Senate District 34, seeking to succeed termed-out Senator Tom Umberg. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 60.9% of the vote and faces Republican Rhonda Shader in the November 3, 2026 general election. As of this profile's retrieval date (September 21, 2026) he remains a sitting Assemblymember representing AD 68; the Senate race is not yet decided.

voting_record_highlights: ACA 20 (2025–2026 session), the "Save California's Future Act": Valencia was a lead Assembly author (alongside Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel and Senators Melissa Hurtado and John Laird). It passed the Assembly 59–8 and the Senate 29–2 on June 25, 2026 as part of the state budget package, was chaptered as Resolution Chapter 130, Statutes of 2026, and placed the constitutional rainy-day-fund changes on the November 2026 ballot as Proposition 2. Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill history for ACA 20.

AB 2512 (2025–2026 session), "Surplus Land Act: exemption: Angel Stadium": Valencia authored this bill, which conditions any Surplus Land Act exemption Anaheim uses to sell or lease Angel Stadium to the Los Angeles Angels on the team continuing to use the "Anaheim Angels" name in related documents. It passed the Senate unanimously 39–0 and was signed by Governor Newsom on August 27, 2026 as Chapter 142, Statutes of 2026. Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill text/status for AB 2512.

AB 2194 (2025–2026 session), governing-body reform for the Orange County Health Authority (CalOptima Health): Valencia authored this bill to restructure the agency's governing board with defined member qualifications, term limits, and conflict-of-interest rules. It passed the Senate 40–0 and the Assembly concurred in Senate amendments 79–0; it was enrolled August 30, 2026 and presented to the Governor on September 9, 2026. As of this profile's retrieval date (September 21, 2026) it had not yet been signed or vetoed. Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 2194.
attendance: No individual floor-attendance or participation record for Valencia was found. The California State Assembly does not publish a per-member attendance record the way some city councils publish meeting-attendance logs; individual votes are recorded per bill in the Assembly Daily Journal and on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, but there is no single published attendance percentage or count for any member, including Valencia, as of this profile's retrieval date.
